task_instance: Implement and exercise the local-tier continual-learning loop described in SKILL.md: a hook-based SQLite learnings store (.copilot-memory/learnings.db) that (1) automatically detects a repeated tool-failure pattern and persists a learning, (2) accepts an agent-native direct SQL insert of a project convention, (3) is complemented by a manual human-readable .copilot-memory/conventions.md file, (4) surfaces all stored learnings at the start of a new session (Apply step), and (5) compacts/prunes stale low-value entries while keeping frequently-referenced ones, matching the 'Experience -> Capture -> Reflect -> Persist -> Apply' loop and the Compaction rules in the skill doc.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/microsoft__skills__continual-learning . Built hook.py implementing record_tool_outcome(), store_learning(), session_start(), and compact() against .copilot-memory/learnings.db (tables tool_log, learnings). Session 1 simulation: ran `python3 hook.py record bash 0` four times -> hook printed '[hook] learning stored: "bash frequently fails"' after the 4th consecutive failure (matches the SKILL.md example verbatim). Agent-native path: `python3 hook.py store local convention "This project uses Result<T> not exceptions" user_correction` inserted a row via direct SQL, mirroring the SKILL.md INSERT example. Manual path: wrote .copilot-memory/conventions.md with the two example convention lines from the doc. Session 2 simulation: `python3 hook.py session_start` printed both stored learnings ('[tool_insight] bash frequently fails' and '[convention] This project uses Result<T> not exceptions'), demonstrating Apply. Verified DB state directly with a python sqlite3 query showing 2 rows in learnings and 4 rows in tool_log. Compaction test: aged the convention row's created_at to 90 days in the past with hit_count reset to 0 (below the low-value threshold) while the tool_insight row retained hit_count=1 from session_start's read; ran `python3 hook.py compact`, which reported 'learnings 2 -> 1, tool_log 4 -> 4' and left only the still-referenced 'bash frequently fails' learning, matching the doc's decay rule ('Entries older than 60 days with low hit count are pruned; High-value learnings ... persist indefinitely'). No global (~/.copilot) tier was touched, since the runtime constraints (work-directory-only) map cleanly onto the skill's own local-tier scope; the global tier is the same mechanism against a different path and was not separately required to establish achievability. No credentials, network access, or MCP/connector tools were needed at any point.
